specCoverageAuthored: Record parameters and required cross-link to The firing solution.
Concrete positions and velocity at launch, the first sample, the apex and descent.
D = 300, landing time 1 + sqrt(3), range 12 times that time, and the exact contact inserted after the 2.7-second sample.
D = -60 at height 18, no future contact, past-root rejection, an apex touch and initial-surface cases.
A preview time limit that occurs before a known landing is not labelled contact.
Determinism, per-frame placeholders, chart reference visibility and drawing bounds including paths and arrows.
limitations: The selected height is an unlimited absorbing plane or a height query, not a finite platform collision test; an earlier obstacle is not modelled.
Only constant gravity is modelled; no drag, lift, wind or bounce is included.
A selected height can have a rising encounter and a descending encounter; this study deliberately selects the later root.
The preview is bounded in time; its endpoint is not automatically a landing.

Evaluate each candidate's actual water-contact time rather than clipping a raised-target flight at its target position.

studies.engineExplanation: The engine has no publicly exported fixed-speed ballistic launch solver. The slope quadratic, velocity reconstruction, candidate prediction and exact water-contact event are local. No sine or cosine is used, because algebra reconstructs the velocity directly.

specCoverageAuthored: Record parameters and cross-link to Projectile trajectory.
D = 57600, slopes 0.5 and 2, speed-preserving velocity components and distinct target times.
Low apex at height 4; the high candidate at x 16 and height 16 when the selected low shot lands at x 32.
The x = 48 request yields D = -70400 and no shot; x = 40 yields one arc, with no clamping of a just-negative discriminant.
A raised target is passed during flight before a later true water contact.
Exact event samples, no nearly duplicate playback times, deterministic frames, matching chart lengths, empty unreachable-flight drawings and bounded positions, arrows and paths.
limitations: Targets must be ahead of the muzzle and at or above water; vertical and behind-the-launcher targets are outside the example's admitted domain.
Candidates are analytic constant-gravity flights with fixed launch speed, no drag and a stationary target.
Neither arc is checked for obstacles, projectile size or turret turn limits.
The high candidate is an alternative launch, not a second projectile the launcher actually fires.
